findings.summary: the prior-head rows carry lag-one 0.997/1.000/0.999, but the only arm that produced them gives 0.0348/0.1186/0.1131 on white and 0.3666/0.1866/0.399 on drift when recomputed from r-20261115T202148674467-drifting-sensor-sequences/study/efit-white-200-0.0100.jsonl and its summary.json; the same triplet is repeated at :46.

the sentence compares nova's axis RMSE (0.0177 m and 0.0236 m) against imas-efit's 0.0134 m and 0.0106 m, which are that arm's mean Euclidean axis error (verified 0.013397 and 0.010579 against an RMSE of 0.014564 and 0.011599), so two codes are compared on different statistics under one axis-RMSE label.

wall_npz re-implements the limiter-unit read owned by nova/imas/mast_efit_referee.py:836 (read_equilibrium_wall) and nova/equilibrium/wall_mask.py:209 (wall_units_from_ids) and keeps rings[0] only, so a machine description with more than one limiter unit loses the rest.

draw_nulls is called with neither contain= nor other_x_points=, although nova/media/poloidal.py:549 documents containment as strongly advised and draws a second qualified null hollow only through other_x_points, so no null on either panel is admitted against the wall.

the sweep branch names its flux map with the preceding sequence loop's variable sequence and args.factor rather than the sweep's own swept, so a run with an empty --sequences raises NameError at the first swept factor and successive factors overwrite one map file.

the record says paint.py writes the SVG and a 200 dpi raster beside it, but the committed directory holds only the three SVGs; the raster that done_when clause (3) asks be inspected exists only at the reviewed run's study/panels/white-0.png.
STUDY is hard-coded to one run's absolute study directory, unlike every other module here that takes DRIFT_STUDY from the environment, so the reader cannot be pointed at another arm.
